parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no universal-exposure measures (no facility bans, no border/document friction documented, no birth-sex facility mandate), and strong resident-facing climate signals (self-ID since 2017, marriage equality, GI/EI equal-treatment and hate-speech law) indicate trans-respecting institutions. Recourse partially works: arrests followed the 2024 mob attack, and the 2017 attackers were convicted on appeal — though slowly. Deductions: the mob attack itself (one incident, sizeable, but with state response), a dated (2013) documented pattern of police street stops and mistreatment of trans sex workers ending in discontinued complaints — impunity for officers, though it targets a local, street-based subgroup — default birth-sex prison placement with only a petition-based transfer route, and an LGBT-wide (not trans-specific) survey showing fear and concealment well above regional averages, signaling real social hostility alongside acceptance. That mix — functioning but uneven protection, dated police impunity, elevated social fear — sits between the 0.65 and 0.75 calibration anchors, closer to the latter because no traveler-facing restriction or organised targeting is documented.
